Verdict

Cheapest name on the page: 3.1x NTM sales against 6.9x for the hosting pack (TeraWulf 11.6x, Cipher 7.6x, Applied Digital 7.1x) and half the pack's EV/gross profit.

The discount is paying for execution risk on a 481% revenue ramp that is mostly one contract (consensus has FY27 sales at $4.1B from $0.7B trailing) and for $7.8B of debt against $35M of trailing EBITDA.

The number that changes the read is the FY27 revenue line: if it holds, 6.9x sales is $67; if it halves, today's price is the fair one.

What comps cannot see here: Comps cannot see contract concentration or what a GPU is worth in year three; every peer in the table is priced on the same hope.

Verdict

Cheap on earnings: 14x NTM against 24x for the software-and-cloud set (Microsoft 25x, SAP 24x, ServiceNow 30x), at parity on EV/sales and a quarter under on EV/EBITDA.

The gap is the balance sheet: $119B of net debt, 3.2x EBITDA against 0.7x for the peers, funding a 48% revenue ramp that the market treats as a loan to one customer rather than as software growth.

The number to watch is net debt to EBITDA: if the FY27 EBITDA consensus ($50B) lands, leverage falls to 2.4x and the 24x re-rate is $215; if capex keeps outrunning it, the P/E stays a debt multiple.

What comps cannot see here: A peer table cannot price the remaining-performance-obligation backlog or the counterparty risk sitting inside it.

Nvidia is the cheapest large AI name on its own multiples: 15.5x NTM earnings against 37x for the set, with the discount made by AMD, Marvell and Arm; against Broadcom (17x) and TSMC (20x) it is at parity.

The market is paying nothing for the growth (PEG 0.20 against 0.43) because it treats $339B of NTM net income as a peak: 60% EBIT margins on a $619B revenue consensus that doubles from trailing.

The one number is FY28 revenue ($695B consensus); a 20% cut puts the stock at 19x and still under the peer median, so the read only flips if the cycle breaks, not the estimate.

What comps cannot see here: Comps cannot see customer concentration: four hyperscalers' capex budgets decide whether the consensus is low or absurd.

Verdict

Vistra sits at parity on earnings (15.7x against 15.3x for Constellation, NRG, Talen and the regulated names) and a third cheaper on EV/EBITDA and EV/sales, with growth four times the group's.

The gap is a cycle discount: the market pays Constellation 22x for nuclear under contract and Vistra 16x for the same megawatts because much of its fleet is gas and coal sold into a merchant Texas market.

The number is the FY27 EBITDA consensus ($8.0B); at the peer 10.6x that is $194, and every long-term hyperscaler contract signed at a fixed price moves the multiple toward Constellation's.

What was not done

  • Peers were chosen by business line from the universe first, then from outside it where the true peer is foreign or off the Hub (SK hynix, Samsung, Kioxia, Nanya, MediaTek, SMIC, Komatsu, Innolight, Eoptolink, IQE, Soitec). No size band was applied; a peer that is a tenth or ten times the size stays in with its reason printed, and the medians carry the count.
  • Multiples are FMP's consensus and statements, not the Hub's stored tables. The Hub's tag-based peer sets were not used (CW2's twelve breaks are the reason); FMP's own peer list is printed on each card for the record, with how many of its names were kept.
  • The NTM blend is a time-weighted mix of two fiscal-year consensus rows, not a quarter-by-quarter build; for a name whose fiscal year ends within weeks (Broadcom, Micron, Qualcomm, Walmart) the NTM is almost entirely the next fiscal year.
  • Gross margin and net debt/EBITDA are trailing (consensus carries neither). EV/gross profit for the loss-makers is trailing. The PEG uses net-income growth NTM over TTM, not EPS growth, so buybacks are not in it.
  • Forward P/E is market cap ÷ NTM net income, which bypasses ADR ratios and FMP share counts; it differs from price ÷ consensus EPS where the share count has moved (Cerebras, Eoptolink, Fluence are flagged for a 1.4–1.5× gap between market cap and price × diluted shares).
  • Analysts' low · median · high are FMP's price-target consensus across all targets on file; the count shown is the last quarter's. The Hub's own checked-target table was not re-read tonight.
  • Lock-up dates are computed only as listing date + 180 days when the listing is within a year (none of the 23 qualifies tonight: Cerebras's listing date on FMP's profile is the one printed on its card). Secondary lock-ups from follow-on offerings are not on FMP and were not sought.
  • No live Hub page was driven; nothing was deployed; no table was written; no key is printed in any file. The 13 Oct pre-profit page's measures were followed (free-cash-flow burn, runway in quarters) but its EDGAR cross-check was not re-run.
  • The RADAR list read tonight has 24 rows (AXTI joined since the brief was written); BTCUSD is left out as a coin, so 23 cards.
PAGE SPECS · the rules, the sources, the FX, the tools

Rules

CW3 · from the raw FMP answers to every figure on the page. Deterministic: same raw, same JSON.

usage: python3 compute.py <peers.json> <deliverable dir> <universe list txt> [today YYYY-MM-DD]

Rules (also printed on the page):
- ONE forward basis: next twelve months (NTM) = time-weighted blend of the two fiscal-year consensus rows
that straddle the next 12 months (FMP analyst-estimates, annual). w = days left in FY1 / 365.25.
NTM = w·FY1 + (1−w)·FY2. FY2 missing → FY1 alone, marked. No row → "no estimate"; a peer with no
estimate goes in on trailing twelve months (TTM) with a T mark.
- Price and market cap: FMP quote tonight. EV = market cap + total debt (incl. leases, FMP's totalDebt)
− cash and short-term investments, latest quarterly balance sheet. All stated in USD at tonight's FX.
- Forward P/E = market cap ÷ NTM net income (so ADR ratios and share-count mismatches cannot bend it).
PEG = forward P/E ÷ NTM net-income growth in % (growth = NTM ÷ TTM − 1; needs both > 0).
EV/sales and EV/EBITDA on NTM. Gross margin TTM (consensus carries no gross profit). EBIT margin NTM
(consensus EBIT ÷ consensus revenue). Net debt ÷ TTM EBITDA.
- Loss-maker: TTM net income ≤ 0 or NTM net income ≤ 0 (or no estimate). Priced on EV/sales (NTM) and
EV/gross profit (TTM); EV/EBITDA kept only when NTM EBITDA > 0.
- Implied price per multiple = peer median × the name's own figure, net debt taken out for EV rows,
divided by shares (market cap ÷ price). Midpoint = geometric middle of the lowest and highest implied
price. Read: cheap ≤ −15% of price to midpoint… i.e. price more than 15% under the midpoint; rich when
price is more than 15% over; fair between.
